tasks.title: Ordering metals from incomplete displacement data
tasks.prompt: Three clean metals P, Q and R are separately immersed under matched conditions in solutions of their ions. P displaces Q²⁺, and R displaces Q²⁺. A coated P strip shows no visible change in R²⁺ solution. Construct a partial reactivity ordering; explain whether the test establishes P above R or R above P; and propose one controlled experiment that resolves the comparison.
tasks.post_commit_worked_answer: The two positive tests justify P>Q and R>Q for comparable displacement conditions. The data do not order P versus R; a coated P surface can block reaction, and even a clean negative result would need appropriate sensitivity controls. Remove/standardize the coating safely, verify metal and ionic solution identities, and compare cleaned P versus R²⁺ plus reciprocal R versus P²⁺ under matched conditions. The transitive graph contains two edges toward Q but no reliable P–R edge.
tasks.protected_work: Choose the scientific model and independently reconcile at least two representations or observations, including a credible alternative or boundary.

factor_evidence.concept_model_selection: Separate pairwise tendency from untested ordering.
factor_evidence.representation_translation: Translate observations into directed edges P→Q and R→Q.
factor_evidence.reasoning_chain_length: Compose the partial order and identify a missing edge.

tasks.title: Scratch corrosion: protective mechanisms under conflicting observations
tasks.prompt: An iron sheet has two protected regions: panel A has only an insulating paint barrier, while panel B has electrically connected zinc galvanising. Each is scratched equally and immersed in dilute saltwater. Initially B's scratch remains comparatively clean while A rusts. After many cycles B also rusts, even though a remnant of zinc coating is still visible far from its scratch. Evaluate two alternative protection mechanisms, explain how the time-dependent observations can be consistent without claiming that zinc is inert, and identify which electrical and chemical boundary measurements would distinguish barrier failure, sacrificed zinc depletion and disconnected coating.
tasks.post_commit_worked_answer: Paint excludes moisture/oxygen only while intact; a scratch exposes iron and can permit electrochemical corrosion. Zinc both forms a barrier and, if connected and electrochemically active, is preferentially oxidised to protect nearby exposed iron. B's early protection is consistent with sacrificial zinc action, not zinc inertness. Later rusting does not disprove the mechanism: local zinc can be depleted, separated by insulating corrosion products, or lose electrical continuity even while distant coating visually remains. Inspect current electrical continuity between zinc and exposed steel, local zinc thickness and product composition, oxygen/electrolyte conditions, and compare a controlled disconnected-zinc sample. Different distances and time stages require a spatial/electrochemical model rather than a label-based rule.
tasks.protected_work: Choose the scientific model and independently reconcile at least two representations or observations, including a credible alternative or boundary.

factor_evidence.concept_model_selection: Choose electrochemical vs passive barrier model across two materials.
factor_evidence.representation_translation: Translate spatial scratch/coating evidence into local anodic/cathodic processes.
factor_evidence.reasoning_chain_length: Reconcile early and late observations with local depletion/contact.
factor_evidence.trap_exception_sensitivity: Visible distant zinc can coexist with failed sacrificial protection near scratch.
